name: bosnian_01
context: A tweet in Bosnian, posted between April 2013 and February 2015 and collected through the Twitter Search API near the largest cities where the language is spoken. A native speaker labelled each tweet by the emotional attitude of the person who posted it.

versions.analysis_for_next: Version 0 has two main error patterns. First, 77 neutral tweets were labelled negative. These annotators keep the negative label for real distress, anger, insult or sadness. Everyday gripes, hyperbolic 'I'll explode' or 'headache from Monday' jokes, puzzled questions about other people, quoted lyrics or aphorisms, and wry self-observations are neutral. Second, 60 positive tweets were labelled neutral. Annotators label as positive many informational links about constructive or pleasant topics: sport and culture events, skiing season, new coaches, ministers' meetings, academies, budgets for science, warmer holidays. They also label promos and ads for wellness, beauty or food as positive. Neutral is closer to bare data: check-ins, vote counts and incident-free logistics. A third, smaller pattern: replies that are only laughter or emoticons (HAHAHA, :P, xD) without real warmth are often neutral, so the model overused positive on emoticons. I will shift the negative threshold up and the positive threshold for news and promos down, and keep neutral for bare facts, banter and mild gripes.

Version 1 pushed far too much into neutral. Neutral was predicted 341 times, though only about 187 texts are neutral. Negative recall fell from 157 to 86, and positive recall fell too. The gold labels show that annotators treat neutral as a narrow class for texts with no detectable attitude. They label negative everyday gripes and irritation: sleepless nights, exam panic, pimples, annoying people, cynical aphorisms about people, sarcastic remarks, 'POVRAĆAĆU' (I'll vomit) and blocking drama. They label positive playful banter with laughter or smileys, flirting ('zaljubi se u mene, hitno mi je' (fall in love with me, it's urgent)), agreement and affection. Ads, shop promos, TV programme announcements, bazaar dates and plain sports news were often gold neutral, so the v1 instruction to make promos positive was wrong. Headlines about civic progress (NATO, support, agreements) still lean positive. Headlines about crime, scandal, conflict, weapons or lawsuits lean negative. In v2 I make neutral the fallback only when no tone is present. Any tone tips the label: complaint, criticism or sarcasm about people goes negative, and fun, laughter or warmth goes positive.

The three versions so far form a see-saw. v0 (58.0) under-used neutral. v1 (59.2) over-used neutral and lost negatives and playful positives. v2 (55.1) almost eliminated neutral, with recall of 38/187. The gold labels are noisy, but some patterns hold. Neutral covers matter-of-fact self-narration, quirky anecdotes, curious or wondering questions, mild physical hyperbole (thirst, bladder, hair, 'Monday headache'), sayings, quotes and lyrics without first-person feeling, and flat promos or schedules. Negative covers sincere suffering (sleepless nights, heartbreak, sadness), irritation or contempt aimed at people, insults, disgust and bad-news headlines. Positive covers warmth, flirting, affection, enjoyment, agreement or support in replies, praise, and constructive news (sport or culture events, institutional progress, wellness or food promos). v3 aims between v0 and v1. Neutral becomes the default for anecdotes, questions and mild exaggerations. Negative needs sincere distress or hostility. Positive needs warmth or enjoyment, not just a laughing emoticon.

v3 is the best so far (65.8), but neutral is now over-predicted: 268 predictions against 187 gold. 74 positives and 57 negatives fell into neutral. The positive misses are friendly replies to other users with :) or :D (joking along, agreeing, teasing), amused anecdotes, uplifting maxims ('Cijeni one koji te vole' (appreciate those who love you)), and news of political or institutional progress (agreements, NATO, release of an activist, budgets, ministers' meetings, conventions, festivals). The negative misses are wry reports of one's own lasting bad state (pimples, dark circles, unprepared for an exam, insomnia, fighting the washing machine), sarcasm about people or 'kids on Facebook', bitter maxims, and news about death, weapons, scandal or disputes. Gold neutral keeps odd one-off incidents, curious questions, bare sports fixtures or science items, plain ads, and laughter that only reacts. v4 keeps v3's frame and adds these boundary cues moderately, without saying 'any tone' as v2 did, since that wording made neutral collapse.

v4 (64.0) pushed too hard toward the sides, and neutral recall fell from 137 to 78. The broad negative cues ('lasting bad state', 'sarcasm toward people') pulled in neutral self-anecdotes and quips, and the reply cues pulled in laugh-only banter. v5 returns to v3's (65.8) personal-text boundaries and keeps only the news changes, which carry little risk for neutral. Headlines about wins, agreements, institutional progress, festivals or new services are positive. Headlines about accidents, deaths, incidents, scandals or disputes are negative. Laughter alone stays neutral. Explicit agreement, greetings or invitations toward someone are positive. Negative needs sincere distress or hostility. This version is trimmed to fit the 400-word limit.

v5 (64.5) over-used neutral: 288 predictions against 187 gold. Positive recall dropped to 115, because the sentence 'laughter or emoticons alone do not make it positive' pushed friendly smiley replies into neutral, along with cosy contentment ('pod toplim jorganom hehe' (under a warm duvet, hehe)), snow with :) and constructive announcements (photo contests, festivals, food or beauty promos, warmer holiday weather). On the negative side, wry complaints about one's own looks, laziness or bad luck ('ja uvijek najebem' (I always get screwed)), bitter sayings about people and harm-related headlines (weapons, illness, expensive losses) still went neutral. v4 shows that pushing too hard collapses neutral, so v6 makes moderate moves. Smiley or laughing replies to a person are positive, while laughter reacting to a story stays neutral. Constructive promos and announcements are positive. Self-complaints about looks or bad luck and bitter sayings are negative. Odd one-off mishaps, physical hyperbole, curious questions, fixtures and plain listings stay neutral.
next_examples_not_copied: Prvi ovogodišnji snijeg u Sarajevu :) (First snow of the year in Sarajevo :))

versions.analysis_for_next: Two patterns hold across versions. Neutral-heavy prompts (v3 65.8, v5 64.5) miss positives. Neutral-light prompts (v4 64.0, v6 64.8) wreck neutral. Comparing v6 with v3: v6's positive push gained 26 true positives at a cost of 17 extra neutral→positive, a good trade. Its negative push gained 41 true negatives at a cost of 43 extra neutral→negative, a poor trade, because it broadened negative to self-complaints and wry gripes ('Monday headache', 'too much to buy', 'why isn't every day the weekend', celebrity quips), which gold mostly labels neutral. v7 therefore combines v6's positive criteria (friendly smiley replies, contentment, constructive news) with v3's narrow negative criteria: sincere distress, hostility, contempt, disgust and bad-news headlines. It also states that commercial ads, product listings, TV schedules and event dates are neutral, since several gold-neutral ads went positive in v6.
next_examples_not_copied: Prvi ovogodišnji snijeg u Sarajevu :) (First snow of the year in Sarajevo :))

versions.analysis_for_next: v7 (66.4) is the base. Its biggest leak is positives labelled neutral, mostly constructive civic or cultural links (EU ministers' meetings, conventions, education contracts, ski season, health tips) and promos inviting enjoyment (Bodybalance, beauty salon, baklava), which v7's 'commercial ads are neutral' pushed to neutral. v8 widens positive news and narrows neutral ads to bare listings, prices and schedules. The negative section is unchanged, since pushing it further has repeatedly collapsed neutral. This version is trimmed to fit the word limit.

v8 (68.1) is the base. Its main remaining leak is 50 negatives labelled neutral: tired or bitter self-reports ('Noc me dotukla... glava puca' (the night wore me out, my head is splitting), 'ja uvijek najebem' (I always get screwed)) and annoyance at nearby people. v9 adds only a narrow negative clause for real exhaustion or bad luck told as suffering and for annoyance at people, while everyday gripes stay neutral. This version is trimmed to fit the word limit.

v9 is the best so far (68.4). Its prediction totals (positive 211, neutral 207, negative 182) now sit close to the gold totals (225, 187, 188). Most remaining errors are contradictory cases. Laughing replies appear in both gold positive and gold neutral, and pleasant photo links or sports and science items are labelled either way. Since this is the final version, I keep v9 almost unchanged to avoid destabilising it. The only addition is a neutral example: a plain science or sports news link with no evaluative angle, such as a NASA animation. This targets a few items that were predicted positive because of the culture or news wording, with little risk to constructive civic news.
